## Body

**Performance: PASS WITH NOTES**, round 2 (final under C34), at `353be4793b98fe2db5914b2e31c95d5ba029afd1`.

**Round-1 fixes:** strict snapshots now capture each original file's bytes or absence, and invalid/unreadable settings refuse before the Sonnet launch or return submission. Restoration follows every completed attempt path, including submission failure, and relaunch results expose per-home reports/warnings rather than stderr alone. CI covers exact restoration with present/absent keys and absent files, failed snapshots/restores and concurrent edits. The model write/`returned:true` now require a successful attempt plus a settings witness, not merely a submitted command; the late-dialog case preserves the prior record. The documented already-default-at-target ambiguity remains a Known limit, not proven per-seat model telemetry. The model grammar/dialog checks add no launch; peer.md has three separate commands.

**Cost delta:** no new periodic loop, timer or launch site. The unchanged explicit-use path retains the **up-to-15-minute event wait**, **5 + 1.5 + 2 seconds** after compact start, one model submission, one dialog capture and optional recorded `tmux.send-keys` Enter. Existing registration polling and gate-specific operations remain as priced in [round 1](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/pull/215#issuecomment-6758479611).

The corrected read/write count is **per governed home**: a complete cheap cycle has up to **4H whole-file read attempts and 2H restore writes/removals**, H at most two, not four reads total when both homes exist. `--ask` takes only the relaunch half. Missing originals now produce a removal when appropriate; unchanged documents need no write. Protected failure paths now pay their restore I/O rather than skipping it.

Snapshots retain full original file strings during the protected launch/return phase, instead of only the model value. Comparing model-stripped JSON, extracting saved models and serializing concurrent-edit results add repeated O(file-bytes) parsing/allocation. The pending event wait itself holds paths/model, not a 15-minute file snapshot. All settings I/O remains synchronous and byte-sized, without an explicit size/latency ceiling.

Switch confirmation reuses `restore.found` from the restore's existing current-file read: **no extra confirmation read or poll**. The second registry read/write is now conditional on successful witnessed application. New `with_settings` materializes, parses and reserializes the revive response once and attaches H reports; it adds O(response-bytes) work, not a daemon round or another HTTP call.

**P215-N001 remains a C34 follow-up:** shared-broadcast filtering still costs per pending return/global event, and per-use settings/gate latency, allocation and monetary savings are not measured by this CI run. The amended cost row closes the original undercount; no normal-use cost blocker established.
